text: A rocket taller than a fifteen story building just fell out of space, and a giant tower grabbed it right out of the air.
On Friday, SpaceX launched Starship from South Texas, sitting on top of a giant booster.
Minutes in, the booster got a low fuel alarm, gave up on flying home, and ended up in the Gulf of Mexico.
But the ship kept going. It circled Earth fourteen times in about twenty two hours.
Then it had to come home, slamming into the air so fast that its belly got hotter than lava.
About eighteen thousand black tiles keep the steel inside from melting.
It falls belly first like a skydiver, steering with four flaps.
Then, right before the ground, it flips upright and fires its engines to slow down.
Instead of landing on legs, it hovers next to the tower, and two giant arms called the chopsticks close in and catch it.
Most rockets get thrown away after one flight. Catching it means it can be refueled and flown again, like an airplane.
Nothing back from orbit had ever been caught out of the air before. NASA's boss called it almost magic.
